question: When did Bindusara ascend the Maurya throne?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**297 BCE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindusara**, the second Mauryan emperor, succeeded his father **Chandragupta Maurya** in **297 BCE**.
 
• He ruled the Mauryan Empire from **297 BCE to 273 BCE**.
 
• Bindusara is often credited for extending the empire further into the southern regions of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He was a significant ruler in the **Mauryan dynasty**, which played a crucial role in Indian history during the ancient period.
 
• Bindusara's reign marked the continued consolidation of the vast Mauryan Empire established by his father.
 
• He was known as **Amitraghata**, meaning "Slayer of Enemies" in Sanskrit.
 
• His administration maintained the policies and governance established by **Chandragupta Maurya** and his advisor **Chanakya**.
 
• Bindusara ensured stability and unity in the empire, which laid the foundation for his son **Ashoka** to rise to prominence later.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**__

 __
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the **Mauryan Empire**, which was the first empire to unify most of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He ruled from approximately **321 BCE to 297 BCE**, establishing a strong centralized administration.
 
• Chandragupta's mentor and advisor **Chanakya** (Kautilya) was instrumental in shaping the empire's policies and governance.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 
 
• **Ashoka**, the son of Bindusara, became one of the most famous Mauryan emperors.
 
• He embraced **Buddhism** after the Kalinga War and promoted non-violence and dharma throughout his reign.
 
• Ashoka's reign is noted for the spread of Buddhism and his inscriptions, including the famous **Edicts of Ashoka**.
